clue.text: Main road, one skirted by food conveyor

indicators.note: to be skirted by something is to have it running round your edges, so the road and the one go inside the conveyor

parts.note: the alimentary canal carries food through the body, so a canal is a food conveyor
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A trunk road edged by a supply route carrying food lorries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like part of 'Main road', but it stands alone as the definition. The food conveyor is the alimentary canal, which wraps round RD and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal as an adjective means chief or principal, as in a cardinal rule.

clue.text: Vessel, strong but short of metal

parts.note: a cup is a drinking vessel

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: a rich flavour or colour is a strong one

explanation.surface: A drinking vessel strong in flavour but lacking a metal part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the final letter. 'of metal' is the definition because cupric describes compounds of copper.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupric describes compounds of copper, so it is an adjective meaning relating to that metal.

clue.text: In speed it's like an ostrich

indicators.note: In placed before the two pieces tells us one sits inside the other

parts.note: a rate is a speed, as in a rate of knots
the possessive is no letter, so this gives the word it

explanation.surface: A remark that an ostrich-like creature is all about speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' sits at the front but works on the next two pieces. Ratites are the flightless birds with flat breastbones: ostrich, emu, kiwi.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratite is a flightless bird with a keel-less breastbone, the group the ostrich belongs to.

clue.text: Double figures?

parts.note: the phrase usually means a score of ten or more, but read as copies or likenesses of a form it describes reflections and pictures

explanation.walkthrough: 'Double figures' sounds like scoring ten or more; here a double of a figure is a likeness or reflection.
explanation.definitionFit: Likenesses and reflections duplicate a shape, so they are figures that double an original.

clue.text: Mathematician I found among first Persians

indicators.note: to be found among other things is to sit inside them, so the I goes into the run of pieces

parts.note: arch as a prefix means first or chief, as in arch-rival
the Medes were an ancient Iranian people, ruled alongside the Persians

explanation.surface: A claim that a mathematician appeared among the earliest Persians.
explanation.walkthrough: The prefix arch- means first, as in archbishop; the Medes ruled ancient Iran beside the Persians. Archimedes was the Greek mathematician of Syracuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes of Syracuse was the great Greek geometer, famed for his work on spheres and levers.

clue.text: Plan protest

definitions.meaning: a noun for an aim or purpose, the thing you mean to achieve
a verb meaning to raise an objection or argue against

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is an aim or purpose; as a verb it means to raise an objection.

clue.text: Wood loaded on front ole

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Wood loaded on front ole (5,3)': 'ole' is garbled OCR and no source gives the full clue; BRAKE (wood) + VAN (front) is clear but the definition is missing.

clue.text: Vital to have best food, lacking energy

parts.note: the elect are the chosen, the best of a group

indicators.note: lacking means the following letter is taken away from the food

parts.note: rice is a staple food
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tip that to stay vital you need the best food, even without energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The elect are the chosen few, hence 'best'. 'lacking energy' removes the physics symbol from the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Something electric is thrilling and charged with life, which is what vital means of a lively performance.

clue.text: Playing Heart card shows caution

indicators.note: playing suggests performing with the letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a ten is a playing card

explanation.surface: At the card table, playing a heart shows you are being careful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' turns HEART into THREA, and the ten is a card. 'caution' is the verb here, to warn.
explanation.definitionFit: To caution someone is to warn them of consequences, which is to menace them with what will follow.

clue.text: Very little dough for form of bread, tasty one exported

parts.note: pitta is a flat Middle Eastern bread

indicators.note: exported means sent out, so the letter for one leaves the word

parts.note: nice food is tasty
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A pittance paid for a tasty flatbread sent abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one exported' takes I out of NICE to leave NCE. 'Dough' is slang for money, not bread dough.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough is slang for money, and a pittance is a tiny wage or sum.

clue.text: Calling for trouble, affronting HM

indicators.note: affronting is read as a-fronting, standing in front of the next piece

parts.note: care is worry or trouble
Her Majesty is the Queen, ER for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Asking for trouble by insulting the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affronting' is read as a-fronting, standing in front of. HM, Her Majesty, is ER, Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A calling is a vocation or line of work, which is what a career is.

clue.text: Independent printed with new lettering -bold

indicators.note: giving the word new lettering means setting its letters in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A newspaper printed in a fresh typeface, in bold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with new lettering' sounds like typesetting but signals the rearrangement. The stray dash before 'bold' is a print mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means fearless and daring, the courage that bold also describes.

clue.text: Some libber, that girl

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A women's liberationist pointing at a particular young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertha is a female name, so it stands for a girl in crossword convention.

clue.text: Name (English place) carried by parcel

indicators.note: something carried by another is held inside it

parts.note: to parcel out is to share, and a ration is a share or portion
to put is to place

explanation.surface: A good name arriving with a parcel from an English spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parcel' is read as a share, as in to parcel out, not a package; 'carried by' sets the two pieces inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A good name means a good standing, the esteem others hold you in.

clue.text: Classes? Fictions, we hear, present a broad view

parts.note: genera are classes in biology, the plural of genus

indicators.note: we hear says the next word is given by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: lies are fictions or untruths

explanation.surface: Classes and fictions seem to give a sweeping overview.
explanation.walkthrough: GENERA is the plural of genus; 'we hear' turns LIES into the sound -LISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To generalise is to draw a broad conclusion from many cases, taking the wide view.

clue.text: A loud Fellow occupying lecture platform

indicators.note: occupying means filling the space inside, so the pieces go into the lecture

parts.note: to scold someone is to lecture them
f, forte, is the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A loud academic Fellow taking over the lecture podium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lecture' is a verb here, to scold; A, F and F sit inside SCOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaffold is a raised wooden stage, as for executions or builders.

clue.text: One's not fancied, vulgarly suited in yellow

indicators.note: in sets the scrambled word inside the colour

parts.note: or is the heraldic name for gold or yellow

indicators.note: vulgarly suggests a crude, mangled version, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rank outsider dressed garishly in yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vulgarly' scrambles SUITED to UTSIDE, which goes 'in' OR, heraldic gold.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing an outsider is a horse given little chance, one punters do not fancy.

clue.text: Fabric, dull Eastern cover, rolled up

parts.note: a matt finish is dull, also spelled mat

indicators.note: in a down clue rolled up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a lair is an animal's cover or den

explanation.surface: A dull eastern fabric cover, rolled up for storage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolled up' reads the cover upwards, as this is a down answer. A lair is an animal's cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Material is cloth or textile, which is what fabric means.

clue.text: Period with OU interrupts short seminar for 11?

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle, so these pieces go inside the trimmed course
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a course of study is a seminar series
an age is a period of time
OU is the Open University, the UK's distance-learning university

explanation.surface: A period of Open University study breaking into a short seminar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts COURSE to COURS, and AGE with OU 'interrupts' it. The definition points to 11, INTREPID.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid and courageous are synonyms, both meaning fearless.

clue.text: Character copper's reported?

indicators.note: reported means as said aloud, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: copper is a metal, the 's read as is

explanation.surface: A policeman's character, as stated in a report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal; 'reported' gives a word that sounds like METAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Mettle is spirit or strength of character, the quality to cope well.

clue.text: Show surprise?

definitions.meaning: a phrasal verb meaning appear or arrive
a noun for an unexpected event

explanation.walkthrough: As a verb, to turn up is to show; as a noun, a turn-up is a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive is to make an appearance; an upset result is an unexpected one.

clue.text: Watch recording seconds primarily

indicators.note: primarily means at the start, so the seconds letter is placed before the recording

parts.note: an entry is a record in a log or diary

explanation.surface: A watch recording the seconds as its main function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' is a guard here, not a timepiece; 'primarily' puts S, for seconds, at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is a guard on duty, as is a sentry posted at a gate.

clue.text: Anchor fleet at destination, briefly

parts.note: fleet means swift, which is fast

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: the end is the destination or final point

explanation.surface: Mooring the navy at its port of call for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleet' is an adjective, fast, not a navy; 'briefly' cuts END to EN.
explanation.definitionFit: To anchor something is to secure it firmly in place.

clue.text: Perused a machine's rotary part that's guaranteed

indicators.note: rotary suggests turning round, so the hidden letters are read backwards
part says only a piece of the preceding words is taken

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone reads up on a machine's rotating component to check it is under warranty.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'part that's guaranteed' as the definition, but 'part' is the hidden-word signal beside 'rotary'; 'that's' is the link and 'guaranteed' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Made sure means ensured or secured, the past tense of to ensure.

clue.text: Dictate from old Right European' in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the word is given as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark

explanation.surface: Giving orders based on an old European's way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: O and R are abbreviations; 'in speech' gives the sound of DANE, spelt DAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to decree or order, which is what to dictate means.

clue.text: Unique, giri's cape, in colour

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, plus the possessive s

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation inside the colour

parts.note: a tint is a shade or colour
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A one-off girl's cape in a striking shade.
explanation.walkthrough: Di is a crossword girl, with her possessive kept as a letter; 'in' puts the cape abbreviation inside the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinct means clearly separate and individual, standing apart from others.

clue.text: How night approaches (in a cryptic sort of way)

definitions.meaning: describes the gradual coming of nightfall, getting dimmer

definitions.text: in a cryptic sort of way
definitions.meaning: an adverb meaning mysteriously or obscurely

explanation.definitionFit: Night comes on with deepening gloom; and speaking obscurely, hinting at hidden meaning, is the other sense.

clue.text: To do this is to act with restraint, withholding pound

definitions.text: To do this is to act with restraint, withholding pound

indicators.note: withholding means keeping back, so the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: to underplay a role is to act it with restraint
L is the abbreviation for pound, from libra

explanation.surface: Paying staff too little is restrained acting, holding back cash.
explanation.walkthrough: UNDERPLAY loses L (pound, from libra) to 'withholding'. The whole clue also defines: paying too little holds back pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay staff short is to keep back money owed, which is what holding back pounds means.
